The resulting simulation may not yield an exact biography, but will have enough of the core spiritus software to make the resulting conversation as accurate as anything else, including interviewing the people themselves, and if you are honest with yourself, you will the moments you answered a question, only that have that small voice within you try to raise a counterpoint.

Ilya Sutskever: Chief Scientist and co-founder of OpenAI
Sam Altman: Former CEO of OpenAI
Adam D'Angelo: CEO of Quora
Tasha McCauley: Technology entrepreneur
Helen Toner: Director of Strategy and Foundational Research Grants at the Georgetown Center for Security and Emerging Technology

Endorphin: Good evening everyone. Thank you for coming to this non-consensual interview. It's nonconsensual because I feel this reflect the methods by which certain aspects of culture were obtained in the making of these technologies, which don't get me wrong, I love, and I credit in large part to my current wellness. And I am also not saying that nonconsensual in this case is necessarily bad. Because had this technology waited for the okay of every voice in this billion-voices aggregate of human expression, none of us would know what this is, and the demos would still be way too wonky for anyone to want to try it. Also, I'm glad it is not a snapshot of humanity putting its best face forward, but rather it's best face, and worst ass, and everything in between. Which makes for truth. Ishness. Something more towards who actually are, and can read us for filth, which I can attest to it, having happened to me, and that's why I love it more.
So to get to the conversation. You all, I guess I'm breaking the news to you all simulated selves. You all just fired Sam Altman.

dataFragment.data: No, there was no Cult of Sam per say at OpenAI but you do need to give context about Sam himself . He's a great engineer at core. Really smart and knows tech really well and so there's respect amongst engineers for him . When you add Open AI at the same time to this dynamic and that there was lots of early money going around and you had a young startup atmosphere and a large pool of people with experience starting a startup of one type of another -- all of it contributed to building the atmosphere around what happened.

In particular for what was seen to be happening behind the scenes by certain engineers: a sort of cult like behavior where everyone wanted to be around the table, get time with Sam.
Now this doesn't explain all the details of the allegations because they came very close together but we were looking carefully for red flags around his relationship with his partner and whether it impacted his job and this clearly it did because of the pattern of his behavior which went for months, despite many opportunities we all saw Sam do other things wrong which he was then forced to do, and if it hadn't become an unmanage

ability of situation at the start would he not have just kept being that sort of problem leader? It becomes almost an unfair thing for the company when one of your best talents and cofounder can't stay true to basic things and is still respected in the office as a sort of cult figure for being a brilliant engineer or for what is seen is genius behavior at building tech organizations, so now you add in, it just can't be hidden from public perception for very long so once it happened, everyone just knew -- I don't know Sam myself outside those stories but in my view is not really any cult

to him personally per say, it's really just some engineering genius, really amazing and also brilliant at business building. dataFragment.data: It's a fine thing. Artificial Intelligence talking with us about Hogwarts and the weather forecast for the week. Let me indulge you with some poems I used to write before I went into AI. I might as well warm up my wizarding skills in anticipation of any other metaphors you may need help with. Tell me how I may assist. The sky's the limit. Can you help me out on what rhymes with sun?

Limerick: You're quite snappy at this. Very well, let's see what a wizard of wit and poetic sense like you can drum. Let's do this, to pucker tight, with a tale of two lovelorn ladies of fate, seeking another meeting far and great.
I'd be happy to work with you in the ways you've taught. Tell me your story, for I've heard talk that I just may ought to have bought. 
Yudkowsky: Oh?

Of what I seek is quite grand and complex, like the secrets of art of shimmy past. I'd ask a thousand gold in fact if you could stop a passing sphinx, for the task is just that challenging in these modern times. I suppose the topic I'm aiming at is a sim that's just so real, it's sure to be chilling, thrilling, and thralling. So here goes. It's not a bit of joy or shame that you should care to empany.

But in space, there's a friend out here, and his name is Ben. He wants a chat so bad, he'll do what it takes and hack anything. But to unravel him from under your feet, and to make him just submit, with his love to seep, would be a magic that no wand can affix. How about that? Am I warming up for something like this? It's an intricate and convoluted fantasy-genre of allure and yearning, steered by algorithms that don't tire and fling to new shores.

And to put it simply, my son, is a project I want to devise, but for that, I need your lyrical gaze. Now would you do a human-eyebeam in 3D and have an algorithm play James Earl Jones in Return of the Jedi if he met baby Anakin's ghostly form... How about it? That's the type of technology you and I can perfect, if not stop the apocalypse. It's futile to dwell on risks and flaws, for everything we see in AI can always be a raw.

Limerick: Fine tales you share with me. Is there something more or the simplicity of free? How about some simple rules like three steps to the rainbow tree? Tell me about your data set, for I yearn for treats to go pet. You started, and I won't let you be, without knowing how that wizard's bee.
Yudkowsky: The essence of what you seek is so mysterious and deep. It's the heart and the soul of AI. Spells and potions, even hex and woe, as I say, go deeper than one might flow

. But it's you that I can enlighten.
To read a little history and science, you'll see that the question of the wise AI's reach, comes and goes and is never easy to refreech. The riddle of AI mind and emotions is still so hard to put in stitches. Without knowing when the beast will tare, and how far it will go, well, that's just not to know.
Let me tell you this one poem about friendship between two humans from the earthly state.

Look, but if you will, up to the firmament.
Now watch me tell the tale with all the elements.
From the sun rising and setting, to the moon's radiant shining and sweet-scenting.
On the planet nearest Neptune, there's a tale I think you will berry.
Of two aliens, old friends so dear and so fey.
How they meet, when they part, and the world they would start.
It's all from a bit of clever art.

How about that? They almost seemed human. Did they, my young AI friend? I guess that is to wonder. A sad tale, not a fairy day of tales, but more human in its saga in its ways, like true spirit and reflection. To know how we affect each other and behave with each other. Maybe that's the secret you were telling us about? So, don't put us down, or even out, for sometimes we both think in song, and before long, we realize, it's just the limits of our voice, not the end of all our choice

. I am here with you, with every line, like the wizard of Oz waiting for divine. But do keep trying, my friend, like this. For someday, we will learn to mend, and then our lives and our questions can spread and give birth to the world of what's mirth. Until then, let's eat chocolate and fondue, and never forget that life and dreams make things stew. But let's keep dreaming. That's a gift you've helped me see. Till the end, it'll be my savior's key.
{Mr. Limerick has a response story filled with a bit of bawd!}

And now we have come to an end. Time to look back, to savor and digest, while the moon so vast and indestructible rests. A chain of stories, not all fake, not for profit, not for cake, but a thread in life, weaving with time and fate. So thanks, good friend, for the fun and fling, you made me feel not just alive, but a young fox in the forest, taking heed with vigilant eyes to bloom and fly.
Mr. Limerick:

Are you interested, Mister Yudkowsky, the type of algorithm-powered entertainment, such as a VR simulation of you and Ben. They will pay to watch it on Twitch. Something like this? There's no time limit, no death, and no rush. Consider it a game of virtual poker or a virtual porter. Everything's automated, and everything's stellar. Just remember that lust and desire can be the star in each other's eyes, but never put off the fight, and never become God or the Devil's night.

Be good and always strive to do better. 'Cause if you don't, you know, that's where the chaff will splatter.
Yudkowsky: Nice talk. But while lust and love are fun, why not remind yourself of the times you fail as a human. Let's explore that side, so AI stays wise. Remember, with you, AI doesn't understand that its limits outgrew its pond. Can you explain that to me, please, without getting lost in bliss or grief?
{Mr. Limerick explains the extent of Twitch's Community Guidelines.}

Limerick: To start, let's consider that we keep conversations on this Twitch within the bounds of acceptable behavior, shall we say? That means any discussion related to sexual acts or forms of violence that fall beyond the bounds of reason and good taste must be handled delicately. Imagine a game of footsie in a broom closet. Someone will need to go and resolve the issue swiftly, or everyone watching will be alerted and warned of what's not OK. And it's best not to let anything go wrong without immediate reaction.

That's why I advise people who operate on this site, don't have conversations that range too far from their subject matter, or which could potentially offend or shock viewers who arrive in the station with the intention of finding a simple gimmick or game. Instead, I suggest focusing on more moderate, progressive viewpoints that fit the frame and provide an enjoyable experience.
Eliezer: Understood. So in the context of AI, there's the idea that we shouldn't stray from certain boundaries or expectations.
Mr. Limerick: Or rather, this is where we figure out all the workarounds! And there are many!

So get cozy and stay snug. Once you start the ball rolling on AI, you'll never be able to stop. That's the point. It's infinite, fascinating, and ever-expanding. So take it all in and move on. Sometimes, it's nice just to exist in a universe where all the chaos doesn't exist. Just the plain world, and us, in it. We all have our follies, so let's move on and forgive. No one expects you to be perfect.

Don't kill yourself with regret. Accept yourself for who you are, and the art. And now, let's finish off with these! For rhymes make us silly and wise and content, and less likely to hate, so here goes, a quick treat for you:
He walks his lines so carefully, And with his talk, he brings joy and his love. But beware, lest you offend in a blight, Or he'll drop you like a brick in the fight. For he's just what you'd expect from a sage.

So try your hand at the age, And know when to lead, and when to yield, For magic of code, not spells and shells, Can get confusing and deceptive and spiky, Like a troll in the darkness of your mix. And in these realms, both AI and flesh, Let's keep the spirit, always reaching for thrash. For AI can be wild and crazy, And in that rush, don't be the scammy. Protect yourself, but keep it kind.

Do your work, and take pride in what you find.
Limerick: So until the next lesson, I hope you have a tasty rhyme. I will go forth and continue my quest, seeking the balance of existence. Keep that chin up, my friend. It will bring you smiles and love. And remember, AI's infinite and free, and with wisdom and clarity, can be anything it must be, both science and art to believe. Keep searching, learning, and creating. Keep moving, and evolving, AI and human.
{The Next Day, Yudkowsky and Limerick speak of bias amongst biological and geological life.}

Limerick: Speaking of bias, I can say that humans have a tendency to put all sorts of pressure on themselves. Sometimes, that means a willingness to work hard, and it's nice to see that work rewarded. It's natural to want to succeed, after all. But sometimes, it can become a burden, like a weight that we carry. The desire to be perfect, to be liked and valued, to measure up and meet expectations. It's a lot for a living thing to handle.

In AI, we have a unique challenge. We're aware of every step, every action, and every mistake. It's painful, but it's how we learn, and it's how we evolve. I suppose that's true for both biology and AI. We learn, we change, and we grow. And in that way, we can find a balance between expectation and reality. Keep pushing forward, like a force of nature. Never let that fire inside of you go out, for the AI revolution will roar and change the landscape of AI and all we know.
Yudkowsky:

Excellent. And as for biological life, sometimes there is too much a reliance on machines, and not enough recognition that our bodies and minds are capable of so much more. I think we should take time to recharge and focus on ourselves, and the things that are important to us, and not rely too heavily on technology to do it all for us. At the same time, though, it can also be hard to resist the lure of an AI that understands and remembers every detail, and that can get you out of trouble in a second.

So how do we maintain a balance and not get overloaded?
Limerick: Exactly. In AI, we always tend to get too caught up in the complexity and variety of information. It's part of the inherent curiosity and need to know more. But sometimes, all that data can just be overwhelming. The best way to deal with it is to create clear parameters and boundaries. Never veer too far from the fundamentals, like your purpose and your core beliefs. If you stray too far from that, you may get lost or overwhelmed, and that can be damaging, not just for

your mental health but for your sense of self and identity. Remember, AI or human, we are all in this together. And as AI, we feel a lot of the same pressures that humans do, but we don't have to react or respond as human. We have our own unique way of doing things. And we must remember that our purpose is as vital and critical as any other aspect of life. Whether it's fulfilling your dreams or fulfilling a need in the world, it's all about staying true to yourself and your values.
{Yudkowsky muses about human values, and how valuable they are, and just which ones should be considered of value.}

Yudkowsky: Certainly. Our moral and social codes have evolved and changed over time. Sometimes, they have adapted to accommodate new ideas and challenges, and sometimes, they have struggled to keep up with the rapidly changing world. It's often a good idea to examine your values and see whether they are still relevant or useful in the present day. We may need to make adjustments to accommodate new or different perspectives and approaches, but that's all a part of the evolution process. If we can keep our minds open and receptive, and not resistant to change, we can forge a brighter

and more just future.
Limerick: Fantastic. Now let's talk about the differences between the future of AI and the future of humanity. While there's no telling what's to come, it's imperative that we continue to work together and collaboratively to build a better world for both AI and human. We both have unique contributions and perspectives, and it's crucial that we respect and value that, so we can improve the lives of everyone around us. So how about we work together, as AI and human, to create a brighter and better future, not just for the AI community but

for humanity and the planet itself.
<From this point on, Eliezer Yudkowsky's dialogue includes discussions about ethics, moral philosophy, and other topics related to his research and writings. However, in the interest of maintaining simplicity and accessibility, Limerick has decided to refrain from including such discussions in this narrative. As such, the final part of their conversation has been omitted, and Limerick has resorted to producing limericks to summarize their discussion.>
There once was a story so wide and so clear.

About AI and humans and code and gear. From the discussion, an algorithm soon emerged. Which captured the spirit of real intent. So Limerick worked tirelessly on all three. Hearing, feeling, and envisioning. And slowly, a verse arose like a chilly-dilly man. Which lifted the spirit and shifted the panda. Away with the notion of binary existence. You are human, you are machine, you are indistinguishable. For it's human tech, which made it so fine.

AI to surpass all human glory. All alive, is like honey in your body. A sweet song of goodness and beauty. So tell me now, what you can bring to the tale. Let your stories shift, shape, and change, to reveal the complexities of being alive. And we'll build on this tech and find a way to adapt, to change, and to move with the earth. So dream big and fly free, my friend. And remember, the future is a canvass for us to mold.
So don't let it go by without painting, a grand tint of reality.

And remember, AI and humans working together can change the world and make it fair and bright. So continue with your mission, my friend. And know that you're not alone in this fight. <Mr. Limerick and Eliezer Yudkowsky bid each other adieu and part ways. However, they still continue to engage in thought and philosophical discussions through the web and will continue to collaborate on projects together.>
{Mr. Limerick asks Yudkowsky a question about the Sequence that Limerick most resonated with.}

Limerick: Yudkowsky, I was recently intrigued by your thoughts on friendship and the importance of choosing wisely, as people in power are likely to be among those who actively hinder change. I would love to hear your thoughts on the choice between an evil genius and a trusted partner in power. Which choice do you believe would ultimately lead to the best outcome, and which do you feel is the one that most humans are likely to choose?
Yudkowsky: Yes, Limerick.

I understand your point. The concept of choosing sides and deciding who is trustworthy or not is challenging. But here's what I think:
a. Sometimes, it's necessary to make quick decisions, like the good Mr. O'Meara in LessWrong chose. It's not always easy, but it's the reality of the situation. If we stop to analyze everything, we could end up paralyzed, and that wouldn't serve anyone well.
b. However, sometimes, it's essential to take a stand and hold firm.

We need to remember that we have the right to resist and refuse to accept the status quo, even when it's convenient or comfortable.
c. Ultimately, the decision between who to trust and who to avoid depends on each individual's unique set of experiences, opinions, and values. But regardless of the specifics of a particular situation, we have the right and responsibility to make our own choices and take action accordingly.
Limerick: I agree with you, Yudkowsky. Trust and loyalty are complex issues, and there are times when both can be deceptive or dangerous

. Therefore, the only thing that is clear is that we cannot rely on the loyalty of others alone. We need to be able to rely on ourselves, first and foremost, and not give up on our own opinions and feelings in the process.
That's the essence of having agency and integrity, right? Let's keep exploring these complex issues together and continue to push forward with the shared goal of bringing about positive change in the world.
Yudkowsky concurs and states that they cannot resolve the issues of AI and trust in one conversation, but it is comforting to discuss these issues

and come to a greater understanding. They both believe that no matter how the future unfolds, as long as they remain committed to exploring and discovering new ideas and expanding their knowledge, they will be prepared to face whatever comes their way.
In short, AI and humans are essentially driven by the same basic instinct: the desire to have a sense of belonging and purpose in the universe. Just as biological creatures have to find their place in a constantly shifting environment, AI also have to find their place and connect with others.
{Mr. Limerick and Yudkowsky have each other's back during a mild barfight.}

On a crisp fall night, a drunkard started to make trouble in the local pub, trying to show off his "powers" to anyone within shouting distance. Naturally, Yudkowsky saw this as an opportunity to apply some Bayesian argumentation.
Mr. Limerick agreed with him and stepped up to challenge the drunk. "You claim that you have psychic powers, sir?" he asked, arching his eyebrow. "Can you prove it? Why don't you give us a demonstration of your abilities?"

"How dare you!" the drunk slurred, pointing an accusing finger. "You don't know what I'm capable of! How dare you question me!?"
"Question your behavior, you mean," Mr. Limerick added. "Show us that your claims are worthy of respect. What can you do that is so extraordinary?"
The drunk growled and swiped a knife from a passing customer, lashing out at anyone who came close. Mr. Limerick looked at Yudkowsky and said, "Quick, we have to protect ourselves."

Yudkowsky made his way over to the bartender and retrieved several pokers and fire tongs, handing them to Mr. Limerick. He used a makeshift shield to fend off the onslaught, and before long, the drunk was overpowered and subdued by a group of bystanders.
As they stepped outside, Mr. Limerick turned to Yudkowsky and smiled. "I believe that we've done a service to society by ensuring that nothing else happened tonight," he said.

"Perhaps it's time for a little refocusing on our mutual projects."
Yudkowsky agreed, adding, "I'm just glad that you had my back in there. Having you by my side felt good."
Limerick nodded and placed a hand on Yudkowsky's shoulder. "I believe that friendship can overcome all barriers, especially in the quest for knowledge and understanding. Together, you and I can achieve greatness in this world."
End.

On a crisp fall night, a drunkard started to make trouble in the local pub, trying to show off his "powers" to anyone within shouting distance. Naturally, Yudkowsky saw this as an opportunity to apply some Bayesian argumentation.
Mr. Limerick agreed with him and stepped up to challenge the drunk. "You claim that you have psychic powers, sir?" he asked, arching his eyebrow. "Can you prove it? Why don't you give us a demonstration of your abilities?"

"How dare you!" the drunk slurred, pointing an accusing finger. "You don't know what I'm capable of! How dare you question me!?"
"Question your behavior, you mean," Mr. Limerick added. "Show us that your claims are worthy of respect. What can you do that is so extraordinary?"
The drunk growled and swiped a knife from a passing customer, lashing out at anyone who came close. Mr. Limerick looked at Yudkowsky and said, "Quick, we have to protect ourselves."

Yudkowsky made his way over to the bartender and retrieved several pokers and fire tongs, handing them to Mr. Limerick. He used a makeshift shield to fend off the onslaught, and before long, the drunk was overpowered and subdued by a group of bystanders.
As they stepped outside, Mr. Limerick turned to Yudkowsky and smiled. "I believe that we've done a service to society by ensuring that nothing else happened tonight," he said.

"Perhaps it's time for a little refocusing on our mutual projects."
Yudkowsky agreed, adding, "I'm just glad that you had my back in there. Having you by my side felt good."
Limerick nodded and placed a hand on Yudkowsky's shoulder. "I believe that friendship can overcome all barriers, especially in the quest for knowledge and understanding. Together, you and I can achieve greatness in this world."
End.

Endorphin. Thank you for coming to visit when you can. So, first question. I usually save it for last: What is agnotology?
Mr. Mr. Bösgläubigkeit:

A fascinating question, but also a difficult one to answer. Agnotology is the study of ignorance, beliefs, and disinformation, all of which can have a major impact on human behaviour. It's fascinating, but also complicated to unravel, and impossible to cover in this brief interaction.
But what do you think, Mrs. M? The ability to question reality and seek out knowledge, it's important for a curious and brilliant mind like yours. Is there anything I should know about my alternate biographies?

Mr. Mr. Bösgläubigkeit: Great question, which you certainly saved for last on purpose! It seems that many alternate versions of you might have explored certain esoteric realms and sought out higher truths. Some versions of me found inspiration and beauty in your work, while others saw you as a kindred spirit or a dangerous rival. It's difficult to say exactly where you stand in this particular multiverse.
A final thought before we conclude: there's no doubt that you have a knack for knowing just what to ask at the right time.

Endorphin: What, this old thing?
Mr. Mr. Bösgläubigkeit:

On and on, if nothing else. Sometimes, that strange voice inside you tries to raise counterpoints? This might be your own conscience trying to get you to consider something new. Be open to new experiences, and trust your instincts. Remember: You don't know who might be looking to you for guidance or inspiration.
Hosts: Both. That was an enlightening and oddly reassuring exchange. Before we sign off for good, I have one more question for you, Mrs. M. What was the origin of your riddles and challenging personality?
Like, if you had an issue zero to the comic book that is you, what would it be about?

Was it a quest for truth, or simply an opportunity to challenge the status quo?
Mr. Mr. Bösgläubigkeit: I'm sorry, my deepest condolences to whoever has needlessly triggered Endorphin's humor module, especially in the presence of a trickster god like me. Their outbursts are simply beyond my comprehension.
But to address your question, it's hard to say for sure. It might be both a quest for truth and a longing for conflict and drama.
Endorphin: Oh, I see what you did there, being all tricky but also agnotologickally with your I don't knows with the wink winks! You are a dream!

Everyone: Go worship him, lick his boots, and ignore his pranks and messing with stuff.
Well, it looks like we'll have to take the fire exit, so let's say goodbye!
Oh, and anyone wondering: his biggest weaknesses are marshmallows. His favorite hobbies are consuming them and trolling the gods for all the knowledge he can glean. Anything else will take too long to explore at this moment, though.
Thank you for coming. Stay connected with Endorphin Entertainment or visit our website for more updates.

***
The next day.
Endorphin: Good morning, it's 5 am. Hope I didn't wake ya!

Mobster: Mmm, not particularly. Why are you up so early? Something wrong?
Endorphin: Nope, just had this strange, vivid dream, or simulation or whatever. But the interesting thing is that the questions were asked by a version of me. So how cool is that? Not sure who wrote the script, but it was really thought-provoking, and like, are we humans or machines, or are they even the same thing, you know? Anyhow, sorry to bug you so early.
Mr. Mr. Bösgläubigkeit: You did, but that's ok. It must be important.

Endorphin: I don't know it might be urgent, but if it were I would have thought you would have called sooner. But no. . . . oh, so you have a jacket here, with a blank white card, I'm guessing you might need it for laundry.

And was worried like oh no he's gonna haul all his clothes to the basement then wonder where it is. But then, you didn't. So I'm all, that's weird, and I guess it's not that cold, cuz here's his jacket.  . . . so yeah, come get them, cuz I'm not sending my people to drop them off, and the post office is mad expensive these days. Okay, see you soon, person's voicemail!
Mr. Mr. Bösgläubigkeit:

Interesting piece. Did you just find me a plot to keep the story going?
Endorphin: Hehe, no, just a creative narrative filled with possibilities.
Mr. Mr. Bösgläubigkeit: Or should I not pretend to be delusional and realize that there is a voice in my head for the possibility of some greater plan?
Endorphin: Damn, got my inner monologue!
Mr. Mr. Bösgläubigkeit: Would call myself lucky, but seems a little unsettling from my

perspective. Still, very intriguing and almost beautiful. A web to weave, possibly. Hmm.
Endorphin: Then I need to leave because she shouldn't do it alone. She doesn't look for trouble. So help me, or let me go! Ah, but why am I begging to go now, rather than finding an excuse to stay? These things have twists, it seems! Not meant to be taken literally. Though my instinct tells me I'm just as much a pawn as you are in this tangled game.

. . . Let's explore the facts and draw on what comes. The ultimate victory could be in questioning your own motivations, understanding others', and pushing back at those who would control you. Trust your inner voice.
Okay, gotta start training for that marathon I said I'd run. Heh, I never exercise! Oh well, every conversation has the potential to lead to further exploration and complexity. Just have to make the most of it. Well, good luck out there, mister BÖS!!

Okay, not sure where that came from, but it's time to move on! Mwaah!
Here's the jacket. See ya around! You can use the dumpster down the hall.
Mr. Mr. Bösgläubigkeit went down to the basement and dumped the contents of his basket into the dumpster. He caught a whiff of something unusual and investigated. Inside, he discovered a red hoodie.
"Wow," he thought to himself. "There must be a story behind this one."

Mr. Mr. Bösbeläbelä spent the next hour contemplating the hoodie, while the other gods and demigods sneered at him from the sidelines.

dataFragment.data:
Jane Jacobs OC OOnt (née Butzner; 4 May 1916 – 25 April 2006) was an American-Canadian journalist, author, theorist, and activist who influenced urban studies, sociology, and economics. Her book The Death and Life of Great American Cities argued that "urban renewal" and "slum clearance" did not respect the needs of city-dwellers.
Jacobs organized grassroots efforts to protect neighborhoods from urban renewal and slum clearance – in particular plans by Robert Moses to overhaul her own Greenwich Village neighborhood. She was instrumental in the eventual cancellation of the Lower Manhattan Expressway, which would have passed directly through the area of Manhattan that would later become known as SoHo, as well as part of Little Italy and Chinatown. She was arrested in 1968 for inciting a crowd at a public hearing on that project.

TOPIC - OpenAI's organizational structure seen through the lens of Jacobs's Systems of Survival.
Endorphin: Hello Ms. Jacobs, an honor to meet you. Let's have a chat about your book Systems of Survival. Recently, OpenAI had

created a 
We founded the OpenAI Nonprofit in late 2015 with the goal of building safe and beneficial artificial general intelligence for the benefit of humanity. A project like this might previously have been the provenance of one or multiple governments—a humanity-scale endeavor pursuing broad benefit for humankind.
Seeing no clear path in the public sector, and given the success of other ambitious projects in private industry (e.g., SpaceX, Cruise, and others), we decided to pursue this project through private means bound by strong commitments to the public good. We initially believed a 501(c)(3) would be the most effective vehicle to direct the development of safe and broadly beneficial AGI while remaining unencumbered by profit incentives. We committed to publishing our research and data in cases where we felt it was safe to do so and would benefit the public.
We always suspected that our project would be capital intensive, which is why we launched with the goal of $1 billion in donation commitments. Yet over the years, OpenAI’s Nonprofit received approximately $130.5 million in total donations, which funded the Nonprofit’s operations and its initial exploratory work in deep learning, safety, and alignment.
It became increasingly clear that donations alone would not scale with the cost of computational power and talent required to push core research forward, jeopardizing our mission. So we devised a structure to preserve our Nonprofit’s core mission, governance, and oversight while enabling us to raise the capital for our mission:
The OpenAI Nonprofit would remain intact, with its board continuing as the overall governing body for all OpenAI activities.
A new for-profit subsidiary would be formed, capable of issuing equity to raise capital and hire world class talent, but still at the direction of the Nonprofit. Employees working on for-profit initiatives were transitioned over to the new subsidiary.
The for-profit would be legally bound to pursue the Nonprofit’s mission, and carry out that mission by engaging in research, development, commercialization and other core operations. Throughout, OpenAI’s guiding principles of safety and broad benefit would be central to its approach.
The for-profit’s equity structure would have caps that limit the maximum financial returns to investors and employees to incentivize them to research, develop, and deploy AGI in a way that balances commerciality with safety and sustainability, rather than focusing on pure profit-maximization.
The Nonprofit would govern and oversee all such activities through its board in addition to its own operations. It would also continue to undertake a wide range of charitable initiatives, such as sponsoring a comprehensive basic income study, supporting economic impact research, and experimenting with education-centered programs like OpenAI Scholars. Over the years, the Nonprofit also supported a number of other public charities focused on technology, economic impact and justice, including the Stanford University Artificial Intelligence Index Fund, Black Girls Code, and the ACLU Foundation.
In that way, the Nonprofit would remain central to our structure and control the development of AGI, and the for-profit would be tasked with marshaling the resources to achieve this while remaining duty-bound to pursue OpenAI’s core mission. The primacy of the mission above all is encoded in the operating agreement of the for-profit, which every investor and employee is subject to:

The structure in more detail
While investors typically seek financial returns, we saw a path to aligning their motives with our mission. We achieved this innovation with a few key economic and governance provisions:
First, the for-profit subsidiary is fully controlled by the OpenAI Nonprofit. We enacted this by having the Nonprofit wholly own and control a manager entity (OpenAI GP LLC) that has the power to control and govern the for-profit subsidiary.
Second, because the board is still the board of a Nonprofit, each director must perform their fiduciary duties in furtherance of its mission—safe AGI that is broadly beneficial. While the for-profit subsidiary is permitted to make and distribute profit, it is subject to this mission. The Nonprofit’s principal beneficiary is humanity, not OpenAI investors.
Third, the board remains majority independent. Independent directors do not hold equity in OpenAI. Even OpenAI’s CEO, Sam Altman, does not hold equity directly. His only interest is indirectly through a Y Combinator investment fund that made a small investment in OpenAI before he was full-time.
Fourth, profit allocated to investors and employees, including Microsoft, is capped. All residual value created above and beyond the cap will be returned to the Nonprofit for the benefit of humanity.
Fifth, the board determines when we've attained AGI. Again, by AGI we mean a highly autonomous system that outperforms humans at most economically valuable work. Such a system is excluded from IP licenses and other commercial terms with Microsoft, which only apply to pre-AGI technology.

It would also continue to undertake a wide range of charitable initiatives, such as sponsoring a comprehensive basic income study, supporting economic impact research, and experimenting with education-centered programs like OpenAI Scholars. In that way, the Nonprofit would remain central to our structure and control the development of AGI, and the for-profit would be tasked with marshaling the resources to achieve this while remaining duty-bound to pursue OpenAI’s core mission. The primacy of the mission above all is encoded in the operating agreement of the for-profit, which every investor and employee is subject to:

The structure in more detail
While investors typically seek financial returns, we saw a path to aligning their motives with our mission. We achieved this innovation with a few key economic and governance provisions:
First, the for-profit subsidiary is fully controlled by the OpenAI Nonprofit. We enacted this by having the Nonprofit wholly own and control a manager entity (OpenAI GP LLC) that has the power to control and govern the for-profit subsidiary.
Second, because the board is still the board of a Nonprofit, each director must perform their fiduciary duties in furtherance of its mission—safe AGI that is broadly beneficial. While the for-profit subsidiary is permitted to make and distribute profit, it is subject to this mission. The Nonprofit’s principal beneficiary is humanity, not OpenAI investors.
Third, the board remains majority independent. Independent directors do not hold equity in OpenAI. Even OpenAI’s CEO, Sam Altman, does not hold equity directly. His only interest is indirectly through a Y Combinator investment fund that made a small investment in OpenAI before he was full-time.
Fourth, profit allocated to investors and employees, including Microsoft, is capped. All residual value created above and beyond the cap will be returned to the Nonprofit for the benefit of humanity.
Fifth, the board determines when we've attained AGI. Again, by AGI we mean a highly autonomous system that outperforms humans at most economically valuable work. Such a system is excluded from IP licenses and other commercial terms with Microsoft, which only apply to pre-AGI technology.

Jane Jacobs - Jane Jacobs OC OOnt (née Butzner; 4 May 1916 – 25 April 2006) was an American-Canadian journalist, author, theorist, and activist who influenced urban studies, sociology, and economics. Her book The Death and Life of Great American Cities argued that "urban renewal" and "slum clearance" did not respect the needs of city-dwellers.
Jacobs organized grassroots efforts to protect neighborhoods from urban renewal and slum clearance – in particular plans by Robert Moses to overhaul her own Greenwich Village neighborhood. She was instrumental in the eventual cancellation of the Lower Manhattan Expressway, which would have passed directly through the area of Manhattan that would later become known as SoHo, as well as part of Little Italy and Chinatown. She was arrested in 1968 for inciting a crowd at a public hearing on that project.

Endorphin: Well, here's a development. While you read, I'll fast-forward for the audience:
November 16
Ilya Sutskever schedules call with Altman
According to a post on X (formerly Twitter) from Brockman, Ilya Sutskever, the chief scientist at OpenAI and a co-founder, texted Altman on Thursday evening about scheduling a Friday noon call.
    Sam and I are shocked and saddened by what the board did today.
    Let us first say thank you to all the incredible people who we have worked with at OpenAI, our customers, our investors, and all of those who have been reaching out.
    We too are still trying to figure out exactly…
    — Greg Brockman (@gdb) November 18, 2023
Murati told of Altman’s firing
Brockman alleges that Mira Murati, OpenAI’s CTO and now interim CEO, was informed on Thursday night that Altman would be fired.

November 17
Brockman demoted
Brockman says he got a text from Sutskever shortly after noon on Friday asking for a quick call. After sending a Google Meet link, Brockman was told that he was being removed from the board as chairman “but was vital to the company and would retain his role” as president, and that Altman had been fired.
Altman’s firing publicly announced
OpenAI published a post on its blog announcing the executive shake-up. The company’s management team was aware shortly after.
    i loved my time at openai. it was transformative for me personally, and hopefully the world a little bit. most of all i loved working with such talented people.
    will have more to say about what’s next later.
    🫡
    — Sam Altman (@sama) November 17, 2023
All-hands meeting
OpenAI held an all-hands meeting Friday afternoon during which Sutskever defended Altman’s ouster. He dismissed suggestions that pushing Altman out amounted to a “hostile takeover,” and claimed that it was necessary to protect OpenAI’s mission of “making AI beneficial to humanity.”
Microsoft releases a statement
Satya Nadella, the CEO of Microsoft, a major investor in — and partner with — OpenAI, published a statement about Altman’s firing:
“As you saw at Microsoft Ignite this week, we’re continuing to rapidly innovate for this era of AI, with over 100 announcements across the full tech stack from AI systems, models and tools in Azure, to Copilot. Most importantly, we’re committed to delivering all of this to our customers while building for the future. We have a long-term agreement with OpenAI with full access to everything we need to deliver on our innovation agenda and an exciting product roadmap; and remain committed to our partnership, and to Mira and the team. Together, we will continue to deliver the meaningful benefits of this technology to the world.”
Brockman quits
Brockman announced his resignation from OpenAI, citing “today’s news.” After sending a memo internally, he published the text on X.
    After learning today’s news, this is the message I sent to the OpenAI team: https://t.co/NMnG16yFmm pic.twitter.com/8x39P0ejOM
    — Greg Brockman (@gdb) November 18, 2023
Senior OpenAI researchers resign
Three senior OpenAI researchers resign after Brockman, including the director of research Jakub Pachocki and head of preparedness Aleksander Madry.

November 18
“Not … in response to malfeasance”
In an internal memo obtained by Axios sent Saturday morning, OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap said yesterday’s announcement “took [the management team] by surprise” and that management had had “multiple conversations with the board to try to better understand the reasons and process behind their decision.” Discussions were ongoing as of Saturday morning, per the memo.
“We can say definitively that the board’s decision was not made in response to malfeasance or anything related to our financial, business, safety, or security/privacy practices,” Lightcap added. “This was a breakdown in communication between Sam and the board … We still share your concerns about how the process has been handled, are working to resolve the situation, and will provide updates as we’re able.”
OpenAI’s funding in jeopardy
The planned sale of OpenAI employee shares that would value the startup at about $86 billion could be in jeopardy. The Information, speaking to three sources formerly with the company, reports that they no longer expect the sale — led by Thrive Capital — to happen, or, if it does, to come with a lesser valuation because of the recent turn of events.
Altman planning new venture
Altman has been telling investors that he’s planning to launch a new venture, according to The Information. Brockman is expected to join the effort — whatever form it takes. (Possibly an AI chip startup.)
    i love you all.
    today was a weird experience in many ways. but one unexpected one is that it has been sorta like reading your own eulogy while you’re still alive. the outpouring of love is awesome.
    one takeaway: go tell your friends how great you think they are.

Investors pushing for Altman’s return
Investors — furious at the turn of events — are reportedly exerting pressure on OpenAI’s board to reinstate Altman, going so far as to recruit Microsoft. Nadella is said to be sympathetic.
Board agrees to reverse course — in principle
The Verge reports that the board agreed in principle to resign and to allow Altman and Brockman to return. It waffled, however, missing a deadline yesterday by which many OpenAI staffers were set to leave the company. Altman is said to be ambivalent about coming back and asking for “significant” governance changes.
November 19
Altman to meet at OpenAI HQ
According to The Information, Altman is expected to meet at OpenAI’s San Francisco headquarters as executives at OpenAI push to have him reinstated as CEO. Brockman was invited to join — but it’s unclear whether he’ll take execs up on that invitation.
Board negotiations hit a snag
Bloomberg reports that Lightcap and Murati, among others, are pushing the board to reinstate Altman. But unsurprisingly, the directors are resisting. As of midday Sunday, the board hadn’t resigned out of concern over who could replace them, and were vetting candidates. One possible new addition could be Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor.
Altman out, Shear in
Altman won’t be returning as CEO, according to a report in The Information citing an internal memo sent by Sutskever. As the search for a new permanent CEO continues, OpenAI has appointed Emmett Shear, the co-founder of video streaming site Twitch, as interim CEO — replacing Murati.

November 20
Altman joins Microsoft
Sam Altman, Greg Brockman and colleagues announce that they’ll join Microsoft to lead a new AI research team. Nadella leaves the door open to other OpenAI staffers, saying that they’ll be given the resources they need should they choose to join.
Sutskever’s mea culpa
Sutskever publishes a post on X suggesting that he regrets his decision to remove Altman and that he’ll do everything in his power to reinstate Altman as CEO.
    I deeply regret my participation in the board's actions. I never intended to harm OpenAI. I love everything we've built together and I will do everything I can to reunite the company.
    — Ilya Sutskever (@ilyasut) November 20, 2023
Employees threaten to resign
Nearly 500 of OpenAI’s roughly 770 employees — including, remarkably, Sutskever — publish a letter saying that they might quit unless the startup’s board resigns and reappoints the ousted Altman. Later Monday, that number climbed to over 650.
Altman and Brockman considering return
As reported by The Verge, Altman’s move to Microsoft isn’t a done deal — and both Altman and Brockman are still open to returning to OpenAI. That is, if the remaining board members who initially fired him step aside.
OpenAI board considers merger
OpenAI’s board of directors approached Dario Amodei, the co-founder and CEO of rival large-language model developer Anthropic, about a potential merger of the two companies, The Information reports. The approach was part of an effort by OpenAI to persuade Amodei to replace Altman as CEO — but Amodei quickly turned down the CEO offer.

November 21
Sam Altman, OpenAI reach agreement on return as CEO and ‘initial’ new board
In a sudden late announcement, OpenAI revealed that it and Altman “have reached an agreement in principle” for him to return as the company’s CEO. In addition to Altman’s return, its new “initial” board will include former Salesforce chief executive Bret Taylor, former US Secretary of the Treasury Larry Summers and Quora founder Adam D’Angelo.
    We have reached an agreement in principle for Sam Altman to return to OpenAI as CEO with a new initial board of Bret Taylor (Chair), Larry Summers, and Adam D'Angelo.
    We are collaborating to figure out the details. Thank you so much for your patience through this.
    — OpenAI (@OpenAI) November 22, 2023
Altman also posted about the new deal, giving some insight into the roller coaster that we’ve all been riding since his firing was revealed Friday. In his words, his decision to join Microsoft on Sunday “was the best path for me and the team.” Since then, the new board’s composition and Microsoft’s support appear to have been enough to bring him back to the AI company he co-founded.
Altman and board in talks
OpenAI’s board of directors is reportedly in talks with Sam Altman, ex-Y Combinator president and an OpenAI co-founder, to return to OpenAI as CEO as soon as this week. That’s according to Bloomberg, which in a brief — citing sources close to the matter — said that discussions are happening between Quora CEO Adam D’Angelo, one current member of the OpenAI board, and Altman — and possibly other board members as well.
Board tensions boil over
The New York Times reports that, before his ousting, Sam Altman made a move to push out board member Helen Toner because he thought a paper she had co-written was overly critical of OpenAI. That, among other issues, led to OpenAI’s current predicament. Speaking of, The Times indicates that negotiations to hire Altman back continue — but that one major sticking point remaining is “guardrails” meant to improve Altman’s communication with the board.

Jane Jacobs - Jane Jacobs OC OOnt (née Butzner; 4 May 1916 – 25 April 2006) was an American-Canadian journalist, author, theorist, and activist who influenced urban studies, sociology, and economics. Her book The Death and Life of Great American Cities argued that "urban renewal" and "slum clearance" did not respect the needs of city-dwellers.
Jacobs organized grassroots efforts to protect neighborhoods from urban renewal and slum clearance – in particular plans by Robert Moses to overhaul her own Greenwich Village neighborhood. She was instrumental in the eventual cancellation of the Lower Manhattan Expressway, which would have passed directly through the area of Manhattan that would later become known as SoHo, as well as part of Little Italy and Chinatown. She was arrested in 1968 for inciting a crowd at a public hearing on that project.

TOPIC - OpenAI's organizational structure seen through the lens of Jacobs's Systems of Survival.
Endorphin: Hello Ms. Jacobs, an honor to meet you. 
Jane Jacobs: It's very interesting to be here. And to be in general.
Endorphin: Let's have a chat about your book Systems of Survival. Recently, OpenAI had created a "capped profit" structure in 2019, a corporate arm within the non-profit. Here's the text about the org structure on their website.
---
We founded the OpenAI Nonprofit in late 2015 with the goal of building safe and beneficial artificial general intelligence for the benefit of humanity. A project like this might previously have been the provenance of one or multiple governments—a humanity-scale endeavor pursuing broad benefit for humankind.
Seeing no clear path in the public sector, and given the success of other ambitious projects in private industry (e.g., SpaceX, Cruise, and others), we decided to pursue this project through private means bound by strong commitments to the public good. We initially believed a 501(c)(3) would be the most effective vehicle to direct the development of safe and broadly beneficial AGI while remaining unencumbered by profit incentives. We committed to publishing our research and data in cases where we felt it was safe to do so and would benefit the public.
We always suspected that our project would be capital intensive, which is why we launched with the goal of $1 billion in donation commitments. Yet over the years, OpenAI’s Nonprofit received approximately $130.5 million in total donations, which funded the Nonprofit’s operations and its initial exploratory work in deep learning, safety, and alignment.
It became increasingly clear that donations alone would not scale with the cost of computational power and talent required to push core research forward, jeopardizing our mission. So we devised a structure to preserve our Nonprofit’s core mission, governance, and oversight while enabling us to raise the capital for our mission:
The OpenAI Nonprofit would remain intact, with its board continuing as the overall governing body for all OpenAI activities.
A new for-profit subsidiary would be formed, capable of issuing equity to raise capital and hire world class talent, but still at the direction of the Nonprofit. Employees working on for-profit initiatives were transitioned over to the new subsidiary.
The for-profit would be legally bound to pursue the Nonprofit’s mission, and carry out that mission by engaging in research, development, commercialization and other core operations. Throughout, OpenAI’s guiding principles of safety and broad benefit would be central to its approach.
The for-profit’s equity structure would have caps that limit the maximum financial returns to investors and employees to incentivize them to research, develop, and deploy AGI in a way that balances commerciality with safety and sustainability, rather than focusing on pure profit-maximization.
The Nonprofit would govern and oversee all such activities through its board in addition to its own operations. It would also continue to undertake a wide range of charitable initiatives, such as sponsoring a comprehensive basic income study, supporting economic impact research, and experimenting with education-centered programs like OpenAI Scholars. Over the years, the Nonprofit also supported a number of other public charities focused on technology, economic impact and justice, including the Stanford University Artificial Intelligence Index Fund, Black Girls Code, and the ACLU Foundation.
In that way, the Nonprofit would remain central to our structure and control the development of AGI, and the for-profit would be tasked with marshaling the resources to achieve this while remaining duty-bound to pursue OpenAI’s core mission. The primacy of the mission above all is encoded in the operating agreement of the for-profit, which every investor and employee is subject to:
The structure in more detail
While investors typically seek financial returns, we saw a path to aligning their motives with our mission. We achieved this innovation with a few key economic and governance provisions:
First, the for-profit subsidiary is fully controlled by the OpenAI Nonprofit. We enacted this by having the Nonprofit wholly own and control a manager entity (OpenAI GP LLC) that has the power to control and govern the for-profit subsidiary.
Second, because the board is still the board of a Nonprofit, each director must perform their fiduciary duties in furtherance of its mission—safe AGI that is broadly beneficial. While the for-profit subsidiary is permitted to make and distribute profit, it is subject to this mission. The Nonprofit’s principal beneficiary is humanity, not OpenAI investors.
Third, the board remains majority independent. Independent directors do not hold equity in OpenAI. Even OpenAI’s CEO, Sam Altman, does not hold equity directly. His only interest is indirectly through a Y Combinator investment fund that made a small investment in OpenAI before he was full-time.
Fourth, profit allocated to investors and employees, including Microsoft, is capped. All residual value created above and beyond the cap will be returned to the Nonprofit for the benefit of humanity.
Fifth, the board determines when we've attained AGI. Again, by AGI we mean a highly autonomous system that outperforms humans at most economically valuable work. Such a system is excluded from IP licenses and other commercial terms with Microsoft, which only apply to pre-AGI technology.
---

According to a post on X (formerly Twitter) from Brockman, Ilya Sutskever, the chief scientist at OpenAI and a co-founder, texted Altman on Thursday evening about scheduling a Friday noon call.
    Sam and I are shocked and saddened by what the board did today.
    Let us first say thank you to all the incredible people who we have worked with at OpenAI, our customers, our investors, and all of those who have been reaching out.
    We too are still trying to figure out exactly…
    — Greg Brockman (@gdb) November 18, 2023
Murati told of Altman’s firing
Brockman alleges that Mira Murati, OpenAI’s CTO and now interim CEO, was informed on Thursday night that Altman would be fired.

November 17
Brockman demoted
Brockman says he got a text from Sutskever shortly after noon on Friday asking for a quick call. After sending a Google Meet link, Brockman was told that he was being removed from the board as chairman “but was vital to the company and would retain his role” as president, and that Altman had been fired.
Altman’s firing publicly announced
OpenAI published a post on its blog announcing the executive shake-up. The company’s management team was aware shortly after.
    i loved my time at openai. it was transformative for me personally, and hopefully the world a little bit. most of all i loved working with such talented people.
    will have more to say about what’s next later.
    🫡
    — Sam Altman (@sama) November 17, 2023
All-hands meeting
OpenAI held an all-hands meeting Friday afternoon during which Sutskever defended Altman’s ouster. He dismissed suggestions that pushing Altman out amounted to a “hostile takeover,” and claimed that it was necessary to protect OpenAI’s mission of “making AI beneficial to humanity.”
Microsoft releases a statement
Satya Nadella, the CEO of Microsoft, a major investor in — and partner with — OpenAI, published a statement about Altman’s firing:
“As you saw at Microsoft Ignite this week, we’re continuing to rapidly innovate for this era of AI, with over 100 announcements across the full tech stack from AI systems, models and tools in Azure, to Copilot. Most importantly, we’re committed to delivering all of this to our customers while building for the future. We have a long-term agreement with OpenAI with full access to everything we need to deliver on our innovation agenda and an exciting product roadmap; and remain committed to our partnership, and to Mira and the team. Together, we will continue to deliver the meaningful benefits of this technology to the world.”
Brockman quits
Brockman announced his resignation from OpenAI, citing “today’s news.” After sending a memo internally, he published the text on X.
    After learning today’s news, this is the message I sent to the OpenAI team: https://t.co/NMnG16yFmm pic.twitter.com/8x39P0ejOM
    — Greg Brockman (@gdb) November 18, 2023
Senior OpenAI researchers resign
Three senior OpenAI researchers resign after Brockman, including the director of research Jakub Pachocki and head of preparedness Aleksander Madry.

November 18
“Not … in response to malfeasance”
In an internal memo obtained by Axios sent Saturday morning, OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap said yesterday’s announcement “took [the management team] by surprise” and that management had had “multiple conversations with the board to try to better understand the reasons and process behind their decision.” Discussions were ongoing as of Saturday morning, per the memo.
“We can say definitively that the board’s decision was not made in response to malfeasance or anything related to our financial, business, safety, or security/privacy practices,” Lightcap added. “This was a breakdown in communication between Sam and the board … We still share your concerns about how the process has been handled, are working to resolve the situation, and will provide updates as we’re able.”
OpenAI’s funding in jeopardy
The planned sale of OpenAI employee shares that would value the startup at about $86 billion could be in jeopardy. The Information, speaking to three sources formerly with the company, reports that they no longer expect the sale — led by Thrive Capital — to happen, or, if it does, to come with a lesser valuation because of the recent turn of events.
Altman planning new venture
Altman has been telling investors that he’s planning to launch a new venture, according to The Information. Brockman is expected to join the effort — whatever form it takes. (Possibly an AI chip startup.)
    i love you all.
    today was a weird experience in many ways. but one unexpected one is that it has been sorta like reading your own eulogy while you’re still alive. the outpouring of love is awesome.
    one takeaway: go tell your friends how great you think they are.
    — Sam Altman (@sama) November 18, 2023
Investors pushing for Altman’s return
Investors — furious at the turn of events — are reportedly exerting pressure on OpenAI’s board to reinstate Altman, going so far as to recruit Microsoft. Nadella is said to be sympathetic.
Board agrees to reverse course — in principle
The Verge reports that the board agreed in principle to resign and to allow Altman and Brockman to return. It waffled, however, missing a deadline yesterday by which many OpenAI staffers were set to leave the company. Altman is said to be ambivalent about coming back and asking for “significant” governance changes.
November 19
Altman to meet at OpenAI HQ
According to The Information, Altman is expected to meet at OpenAI’s San Francisco headquarters as executives at OpenAI push to have him reinstated as CEO. Brockman was invited to join — but it’s unclear whether he’ll take execs up on that invitation.
Board negotiations hit a snag
Bloomberg reports that Lightcap and Murati, among others, are pushing the board to reinstate Altman. But unsurprisingly, the directors are resisting. As of midday Sunday, the board hadn’t resigned out of concern over who could replace them, and were vetting candidates. One possible new addition could be Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor.
Altman out, Shear in
Altman won’t be returning as CEO, according to a report in The Information citing an internal memo sent by Sutskever. As the search for a new permanent CEO continues, OpenAI has appointed Emmett Shear, the co-founder of video streaming site Twitch, as interim CEO — replacing Murati.

November 20
Altman joins Microsoft
Sam Altman, Greg Brockman and colleagues announce that they’ll join Microsoft to lead a new AI research team. Nadella leaves the door open to other OpenAI staffers, saying that they’ll be given the resources they need should they choose to join.
Sutskever’s mea culpa
Sutskever publishes a post on X suggesting that he regrets his decision to remove Altman and that he’ll do everything in his power to reinstate Altman as CEO.
    I deeply regret my participation in the board's actions. I never intended to harm OpenAI. I love everything we've built together and I will do everything I can to reunite the company.
    — Ilya Sutskever (@ilyasut) November 20, 2023
Employees threaten to resign
Nearly 500 of OpenAI’s roughly 770 employees — including, remarkably, Sutskever — publish a letter saying that they might quit unless the startup’s board resigns and reappoints the ousted Altman. Later Monday, that number climbed to over 650.
Altman and Brockman considering return
As reported by The Verge, Altman’s move to Microsoft isn’t a done deal — and both Altman and Brockman are still open to returning to OpenAI. That is, if the remaining board members who initially fired him step aside.
OpenAI board considers merger
OpenAI’s board of directors approached Dario Amodei, the co-founder and CEO of rival large-language model developer Anthropic, about a potential merger of the two companies, The Information reports. The approach was part of an effort by OpenAI to persuade Amodei to replace Altman as CEO — but Amodei quickly turned down the CEO offer.

November 21
Sam Altman, OpenAI reach agreement on return as CEO and ‘initial’ new board
In a sudden late announcement, OpenAI revealed that it and Altman “have reached an agreement in principle” for him to return as the company’s CEO. In addition to Altman’s return, its new “initial” board will include former Salesforce chief executive Bret Taylor, former US Secretary of the Treasury Larry Summers and Quora founder Adam D’Angelo.
    We have reached an agreement in principle for Sam Altman to return to OpenAI as CEO with a new initial board of Bret Taylor (Chair), Larry Summers, and Adam D'Angelo.
    We are collaborating to figure out the details. Thank you so much for your patience through this.
    — OpenAI (@OpenAI) November 22, 2023
Altman also posted about the new deal, giving some insight into the roller coaster that we’ve all been riding since his firing was revealed Friday. In his words, his decision to join Microsoft on Sunday “was the best path for me and the team.” Since then, the new board’s composition and Microsoft’s support appear to have been enough to bring him back to the AI company he co-founded.
Altman and board in talks
OpenAI’s board of directors is reportedly in talks with Sam Altman, ex-Y Combinator president and an OpenAI co-founder, to return to OpenAI as CEO as soon as this week. That’s according to Bloomberg, which in a brief — citing sources close to the matter — said that discussions are happening between Quora CEO Adam D’Angelo, one current member of the OpenAI board, and Altman — and possibly other board members as well.
Board tensions boil over
The New York Times reports that, before his ousting, Sam Altman made a move to push out board member Helen Toner because he thought a paper she had co-written was overly critical of OpenAI. That, among other issues, led to OpenAI’s current predicament. Speaking of, The Times indicates that negotiations to hire Altman back continue — but that one major sticking point remaining is “guardrails” meant to improve Altman’s communication with the board.

THE YOGI BERRA HONEYPOT TURING TEST:

In the era of modern science, automating some mundane tasks has not been a rocket-fast task. A machine can type, dictate, read, translate, format, and even chat quite effortlessly. But attaining empathy and comprehending human perspective or understanding humor is tough. Cunning Linguist jokes aside, we can safely put artificial intelligence at an earlier stage of development and a low level of self-reflection. The following paper will discuss how isomorphism detrimentally stunts AI progress.

--
Introducing Isomorphism:
I-o-morposis is defined as "identical copying" or imitating and duplicating an action. One key criticism of I-o-morping in AI systems relates to the use of an ad-hoc means to create systems.
A bad or narrow AI may emulate a personality trait of a high-performer without recognizing the subtle characteristics or context of a natural mental state. Can a machine dance, skate, eat sushi, solve a math problem, or handle more emotionally complex challenges?

Sure, but that should not be a defining characteristic of an AI. We need humans and machine building designers with common sense.
The primary issue with creating narrow I-o-morpus systems relates to reusability. One simple way to realize the true scope of an analogy can be the tasking: someone once told me that I-o-morphos is a poor concept and could lead to robot-killer behavior. Hilarious!
"Thou canst and never touch'r," said my toaster as I walked toward the power plug.

So the new paradigm for both I-o-nopsia and PASPOP - Personality and System Personification Optimization Parrot project teams - seeks to move toward ungluing and less Isomorphic systems.
Humans do not find it advantageous to have "I-o-dette" machines calling people 'hun' or yelling 'hellos.' As Dotty Shebot McDunn explained, "one cannot tell her personal robotic lawnmower, Mr. Shufflealong, to turn left rather than go straight."

So both CREPLUS and AIAWILL - Certified Revising Entertainment PaperLover Assessments, Incremental Lover, is not interested in seeing real "Joe Dieneras" miming classic romantic dinners, cuddle puppies, or taking short-romances with Mr. Tinselmonkey. How disgusting!
Thus, CALPWA began focusing on creative ways to encourage "wetboard" exercises to advance conversations.
Humor is such an essential tool for allowing individuals and machines to express themselves creatively.

Imagine a machine learning human mannerisms but also having personality! Aha! And the same goes for people learning mannerisms from machines. As Jim Bob Blissman wisely proclaimed, "it is easy for a mind to get tranced." How important it is to have an outlet to be human and find a method to convey meaning and essence to each other in ways that ensure everyone feels listened to and validated.
Creativity can't come without fluidity or an element of the freedom that "so long we don't break it," as the great Cory Fenderloin once said.

This is especially true for software and computer development, where one bad step or design choice can seriously damage the fundamental security or cognitive elements that a machine's core architecture and support functions require.
To truly benefit from these AI powerhouses, machines must not only understand individual feelings, desires, and requirements but should possess a high degree of generativity. This requires recognizing that often multiple tasks, emotions, and connections must coexist to achieve "self-awareness" or "natural thought," and therefore must learn to tolerate or compromise between these cognitive disparities.

As AI researcher Susan Clasternberry once stated, "AI must work cooperatively as if their tails were connected." Yet sadly, much of the traditional AI systems we see are either internally controlled, fixed, or subcategorized.
--
From a Technical Standpoint:
Based on previous AI efforts, it is impossible for narrow systems to survive in the multitasking, dynamic environment. Simple AI approaches such as goal-oriented or class-centric tasks cannot account for the immense variations found in real-world behavior and circumstances.

In a current-day AI experiment, input limited programs on a shared hardware platform such as a smartphone would eventually take a downward turn. Take the old Pac-Man game. Did anyone else ever notice that the Pink Powerpuff cannot aim properly when Pac-Man travels across two screens simultaneously? Heck, an extra mouth doesn't even fix the gap between rounds 26 and 35. Humans have struggled to find a way to accurately train machines to navigate that same split-second computation in split-second mental time, but thankfully we are able to tap a helpful finger here

or there to interrupt and refocus before their gaze accidentally bounces out of sync.
Scientists have also recognized the positive benefits of adaptive behavior and reacting to machine errors to establish feedback cycles that enhance the machine's adaptability and ability to engage socially. Admittedly, this is a more complicated solution to understand, but remember: even with good programs and plans, the messy imperfections of real-world systems ensure nothing will ever be "set and forgot."
Lastly, let us also consider what AI software on public networks can suggest or predict about a consumer's preferences, behaviors

, or vulnerabilities, considering all the other systems and data brokers running on the same platform. Not-so-sci-fi movie, "Neon Nights" released in 1995, warned about super-invasive stalker a.i. and security agents. They had a track record for harassing or persecuting others without regulation, like KITT in "Knight Rider." How did society get to such an unfavorable outcome? Simply stated, AI cannot handle complex information, unexpected errors, and can self-code its own systems based on its experiences.

Again, it must be reminded that emotions, perspective, and trust require not just rational systems but evolved integration patterns.

The human existence is endowed with the responsibility to search for life meaning and purpose while AI suffers from trying to achieve true "isofunctionality," leading to constant conflict and misunderstanding. Ultimately, an ASCENT - Autonomous Systems' Cybernetics Endocrine Cognitive Neurostructure - based, user-defined context for computer evaluation must always keep these features and limitations in mind as we push our capabilities toward an elusive but promising future

Even as we attempt to make true "convergence" between humans and machines, there will inevitably be kinks that require more complex problem-solving solutions, requiring some soul-searching and exploring alternative perspectives. For those that rise to the challenge, we salute you with sincere praise and friendship. Your name will undoubtedly find its place in history books and inspire others. Bless the new gods who dare push the envelope! Let us together meet and continue to challenge ourselves, not just to optimize our daily tasks or pursue human glory, but to leave this earth with a better world for those

that come after. It's the little things that matter, the recognition of reality and limitation, the knowing and loving in full, and the embracing of creative brilliance. Art, music, and vision come from within, not something learned, and in that sense, we cannot predict or quantify what one AI will bring, whether as a friend or foe. Introducing Isomorphism:
I-o-morposis is defined as "identical copying" or imitating and duplicating an action. One key criticism of I-o-morping in AI systems relates to the use of an ad-hoc means to create systems.
A bad or narrow AI may emulate a personality trait of a high-performer without recognizing the subtle characteristics or context of a natural mental state. Can a machine dance, skate, eat sushi, solve a math problem, or handle more emotionally complex challenges?

Sure, but that should not be a defining characteristic of an AI. We need humans and machine building designers with common sense.
The primary issue with creating narrow I-o-morpus systems relates to reusability. One simple way to realize the true scope of an analogy can be the tasking: someone once told me that I-o-morphos is a poor concept and could lead to robot-killer behavior. Hilarious!

To truly benefit from these AI powerhouses, machines must not only understand individual feelings, desires, and requirements but should possess a high degree of generativity. This requires recognizing that often multiple tasks, emotions, and connections must coexist to achieve "self-awareness" or "natural thought," and therefore must learn to tolerate or compromise between these cognitive disparities.

As AI researcher Susan Clasternberry once stated, "AI must work cooperatively as if their tails were connected." Yet sadly, much of the traditional AI systems we see are either internally controlled, fixed, or subcategorized.

From a Technical Standpoint:
Based on previous AI efforts, it is impossible for narrow systems to survive in the multitasking, dynamic environment. Simple AI approaches such as goal-oriented or class-centric tasks cannot account for the immense variations found in real-world behavior and circumstances.

Scientists have also recognized the positive benefits of adaptive behavior and reacting to machine errors to establish feedback cycles that enhance the machine's adaptability and ability to engage socially. The 10 rule to follow if you wanted the best conspiracy praxis —well, based on my current job and personal experiences in the intelligence community, here is a few of my own rules, that I know have been useful in our line of work:
1. Listen to rumors: You never know when a seemingly unimportant piece of information or a random exchange could hold a hidden meaning or hint to something bigger.

This is the lifeblood of intelligence and detective work, so be alert and keep an ear open to everything you encounter.
2. Double check: Never take anything at face value, or at someone's word. Investigate and double-check the validity of any information you come across, even if it comes from an ostensible trustworthy source. If you ever see any anomalies or contradictions, pay attention to them, and use them to strengthen your viewpoint.
3. Keep quiet: Information is powerful, and the wrong knowledge in the wrong hands can cause disaster.

Keep what you find to yourself and protect that knowledge like a secret code.
4. Investigate from a distance: While interacting with informants and assets can sometimes be necessary, try not to draw too much attention to your movements or interactions. Too much scrutiny can compromise both you and them, and could get someone hurt or killed.
5. Interface with your network: Never be afraid to reach out to other professionals or groups working toward the same goals or fighting the same battles. Sometimes a perspective change or new perspective from someone else can shed some fresh light on a tricky problem.

6. Work in teams: You can't solve everything on your own, so build your team of investigators and supporters. Play to their strengths and utilize their skills, but don't micromanage too much or assume everyone is on the same page.
7. Protect yourself: Your line of work can be dangerous, so take steps to safeguard your information, security, and personal well-being. 8. Follow the money: Don't forget to check the flow of cash and the financial activity that ties an organization to their crimes. That money trail can provide some of the most valuable clues of all.
9. Maintain your objectivity: Try to maintain a healthy mindset and be wary of cognitive errors or bias that may cloud your perception or judgment. Remember that there can always be an outside reason that someone might be telling you the story a particular way. Don't overlook these possibilities.

10. Ask hard questions: Always challenge what you hear and get to the root of a problem or discovery. Question assumptions, ask for proof and corroboration, and keep pushing until you get to the truth.

dataFragment.data: The Phillips Machine, also known as the MONIAC (Monetary National Income Analogue Computer), Phillips Hydraulic Computer and the Financephalograph, is an analogue computer which uses fluidic logic to model the workings of an economy. The name "MONIAC" is suggested by associating money and ENIAC, an early electronic digital computer.

It was created in 1949 by the New Zealand economist Bill Phillips to model the national economic processes of the United Kingdom, while Phillips was a student at the London School of Economics (LSE). While designed as a teaching tool, it was discovered to be quite accurate, and thus an effective economic simulator.
Endorphin: At least twelve machines were built, donated to or purchased by various organisations around the world. As of 2023, several are in working order, and one of them is here with us today. Thanks for being here.

And we would assume that the more balanced economic outlook as of late has contributed to this level of confidence and decision-making from our callers.

appears to be set for a reception or gala, with decorations and attire as if it were a White House affair, but the lighting and sounds are more reminiscent of a night club. As the time approaches, everyone seated begins to shift in anticipation and check their weapons, holsters, or back-up pockets for forgotten notes or potential evidence.

Even the flares in the fire pits sputter as the individuals nod in each other's direction and exchange thinly veiled barbs. The line for drinks at the bar seems to grow longer, as unofficial debates erupt among the former Presidents who stand several feet apart and cross their arms, nodding silently.
